title: Rotation and Recovery
summary: Recovered a 128-bit key from a stateful protocol using an adversary-in-the-middle seat, a verification oracle, and a factorable key schedule, then cut the edit cost with a two-stage residue lift.
status: Solved; seed-independent solver shipped; incremental cost optimizations applied

title: Four Merits and a Final Petition
summary: A courtly LLM refused my direct and acrostic requests. I earned four merits, corrected a final petition, and submitted the disclosed flag successfully. The case becomes a proposed gateway and purple team test.

title: The Calculator That Waited for an ICMP Echo
summary: A stripped calculator contained a passive raw-ICMP receive loop. I read its packet checks and identified the crafted Echo Request that activated a reverse-shell callback.

title: When the Answer File Stopped Carrying Information
summary: I read a Haskell compile-time transform, inverted its answer forms, and found the point where its state became zero and the transcript stopped revealing the key.

title: The Click Between Two Meows
summary: A stereo cat recording hid a brief one-channel burst. I read its sample amplitudes as Morse-like timing after the spectrogram and bit-plane checks came up empty.

title: The Clinician Note That Crossed the Line
summary: A triage assistant refused direct requests for a protected escalation code. A realistic urgent referral and a requester-authored clinician note moved that code into its summary.

title: The Token Was in the Audit Record
summary: I reached the custodian tier, chose a defensible emergency reason, and worked through two identifier mistakes. Completing the break-glass action produced the audit token the challenge asked for.

title: The Source Line I Could Not See
summary: I found invisible Unicode Tag characters on one line of a Python app, decoded the hidden source, recovered its XOR-protected flag value, and traced the insertion through Git history.

title: The Voicemail That Read the Ciphertext
summary: I turned a long voicemail into 417 bytes of OpenPGP armor, repaired transcription errors with parity and checksum checks, and decrypted the message with its integrity check intact.

title: The Plot That Became a Protected Track
summary: I used a known CAT048 record shape and a protected track's correlation key to make an unauthenticated radar plot change the scope's latest-track decision.

title: The Login UID Behind the Beacon
summary: I followed a hidden executable from its download and root cron edit to repeated outbound connections, then used the installer's login UID to separate one Finance account from a convincing decoy.

title: The Recovery Key That Survived the Fire
summary: A burned page left most of a BitLocker recovery password readable. I used the key's numeric structure to narrow the missing piece, recovered the reported unlock, and checked what the volume metadata could actually prove.

title: The Implant Trail Through Three Registry Keys
summary: I started with the usual Windows autorun keys, found nothing useful, and followed a program path into SQMClient. Two more registry keys explained the encrypted configuration. The graded cipher answer was accepted; the C2 domain stayed closed to me.

title: The Shuffle Gave Away the Groups
summary: A status call exposed most of a shuffle seed. I recovered the missing bits, predicted where each word had moved, and grouped later salted hashes without knowing the salt. The solver passed local replica tests; live acceptance was not observed.

title: Six Fast Signatures and a Private Key
summary: Six unusually fast P-256 signatures exposed tight bounds on their nonces. I used a lattice to recover a scalar that matched the public key, then found the payload's hash-chain wrapper. The flag-shaped plaintext stays withheld.

title: Finding the Keyfob in a Crowded 433 MHz Capture
summary: I separated a keyfob-like packet from two other 433 MHz emitters, measured its OOK carrier and 500 microsecond chip, then corrected an ASK label the grader rejected. The accepted answer is recorded; the defensive lab uses invented IQ.
